title: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
content: PM-KISAN is a central sector scheme that provides income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families across India, payable in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 every four months directly into bank accounts via DBT. Eligibility: Small, marginal, and landholding farmers with land in their name. Application via pmkisan.gov.in or CSC centers.
source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Govt of India

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
content: PMFBY provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks (drought, flood, unseasonal rains, pests, diseases) from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Premium rates are capped at 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops. Farmers can enroll via banks, CSC, or pmfby.gov.in.
source: Government of India, PMFBY Portal

title: Soil Health Card Scheme (SHC)
content: The Soil Health Card scheme assesses soil nutrient status on 12 parameters: N, P, K (macro-nutrients); S (secondary-nutrient); Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, Bo (micro-nutrients); and pH, EC, OC (physical parameters). It provides customized fertilizer dosage recommendations to prevent overuse of urea and enhance soil organic matter. Farmers should test soil every 3 years.
source: Department of Agriculture and Cooperation, Govt of India

title: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) - Per Drop More Crop
content: PMKSY promotes micro-irrigation technologies (drip and sprinkler systems) with up to 55% financial subsidy for small/marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers. Drip irrigation saves 40-60% water, reduces weed growth, and increases fertilizer use efficiency via fertigation.
source: Ministry of Jal Shakti & Ministry of Agriculture

title: Integrated Pest Management & Safe Pesticide Application Guidelines
content: Agricultural Safety Notice: Always follow CIBRC (Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee) registered dosages and read product labels carefully. Use protective equipment (gloves, masks) during pesticide application. Spray during calm morning or late afternoon hours to prevent drift. Avoid spraying near water bodies. Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or district agricultural extension officer for specific pest diagnosis before applying chemicals.
source: ICAR - Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee
